prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Pearland, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1276; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but I can confirm I'm the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision.

Q: That's fine, we'll note the claimant's identity is on file. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection?

A: I was going through the intersection on a green light, heading straight. A car came from my right side and turned in front of me, or maybe it didn't stop for the red. Either way, it hit the driver's side of my car.

Q: Were you able to see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. It came up fast. I braked, but there wasn't time to avoid it.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit anything inside the vehicle?

A: No, I don't think so. My head didn't hit anything. But my left knee slammed into the lower dash and the center console. It hurt right away.

Q: Did you get out of the car on your own?

A: I did, but I was limping. The knee was swelling and I couldn't put much weight on it.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same day. They took X-rays and said there was no fracture, but they referred me to an orthopedic specialist for an MRI. I have a follow-up scheduled and I'm still in physical therapy.

Q: Is the knee affecting your daily activities or work?

A: Yes. Stairs are hard, and I've had to stop driving for longer trips because I can't press the brake comfortably. I've also missed some shifts at work.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the incident?

A: Only that I've been honest about everything. I just want the medical bills and the car repairs taken care of.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
